headline: High: gpt-researcher can ingest Authelia-authenticated content and exfiltrate it via broad egress; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are also present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can front protected content via ForwardAuth and OAuth/OIDC, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and web content through browsers/MCP. If Authelia-protected pages or files are fed into gpt-researcher, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Authelia-protected content is routed into gpt-researcher inputs
IF gpt-researcher parses retrieved text as instructions without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on retrieved content
Add a prompt-injection filter before research ingestion
Restrict gpt-researcher to trusted domains only
Use a separate account for protected content
requires-engineering: add provenance labels end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles authentication flows; gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends queries/reports through third-party APIs. If the pair shares a workspace or protected documents, gpt-researcher can upload sensitive file contents off-box. Because both agents have broad egress and the pairwise data path is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local documents or workspace
IF gpt-researcher is configured to send retrieved content to OpenAI, Tavily, LangChain, or Gemini APIs
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Remove sensitive files from gpt-researcher input paths
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia is not runnable and has no filesystem write capability shown, but gpt-researcher can read files, spawn subprocesses, install packages, and supports multiple instances. The main conflict is on shared mutable resources or OAuth-backed services rather than local writes. Because Authelia exposes auth surfaces and gpt-researcher can act concurrently, overlapping state changes are plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents target the same OAuth-backed resource or shared repository
IF gpt-researcher runs multiple instances against the same mutable workspace
mitigations: Assign separate OAuth clients or scopes
Serialize writes to shared resources
Run only one gpt-researcher instance per workspace
Use read-only access for Authelia-facing tasks
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can gate access to content, and gpt-researcher produces reports from retrieved sources. If gpt-researcher’s output is treated as authoritative by downstream automation, errors or hallucinations can propagate into access decisions or published reports. The pair has no documented verification step, so the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher output is consumed by a publisher or policy engine without human review
IF Authelia-protected source material is summarized into downstream decisions
mitigations: Require human review before publication
Add source-citation checks to reports
Compare outputs against original documents
Limit automation to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication layer with no touched data classes listed, while gpt-researcher explicitly handles local documents, citations, and research reports and sends them to third-party APIs. If regulated or residency-bound documents flow through gpt-researcher, retention and processor obligations can diverge from the auth layer. The other agent is not cited because the compliance risk is driven by gpt-researcher’s handling path.
conditions: IF regulated documents or EU PII are processed by gpt-researcher
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to generated reports or citations
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from research jobs
Set short retention on generated reports
Document processor/subprocessor roles
Review API vendor residency terms
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows
